clinician.final_diagnosis: fatal invasive osteomyelitis in an allo-HSCT recipient caused by RM
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 73-year-old male, 6 months post allogeneic stem cell transplantation for myelodysplastic syndrome, presented with critical septic condition, fever, and dyspnea. Initial microbiologic investigations were negative. He subsequently developed right hip pain. Imaging (ultrasound, CT, MRI) revealed massive secondary osteomyelitis in the right femoral head, neck, and trochanteric region, with cortical breakthrough and surrounding soft tissue involvement, along with bone infarcts (E004). Emergency surgical intervention showed extensive bone and soft tissue destruction with blackened tissue, leading to proximal femoral resection, debridement, and placement of an antibiotic and antimycotic loaded spaceholder (E005). Bacterial cultures from the osteomyelitis site were negative (E006). Microbiological and histopathological analysis, including basic local alignment search tool (BLAST), identified 'RM' (E006). Despite maximal multimodal care, the disease progressed drastically, leading to the cessation of therapeutic interventions and the patient's death a few days later (E010).
